sections.overview: The Sumatran striped rabbit is a rarely observed lagomorph endemic to the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
sections.identification: Its distinctive longitudinal stripes separate it from the introduced European rabbit, but sightings are too scarce for a fuller field description here.
sections.habitat: Records concentrate in the Barisan mountain forests, including Bukit Barisan Selatan and Kerinci Seblat, with some reports from lower elevations.
sections.diet: Its diet has not been established well enough in the research sources consulted to describe confidently.
sections.behavior: Indonesian conservation notes describe it as elusive and mainly nocturnal; camera traps have recorded it moving along forest trails at night.
sections.reproduction: Reliable field information on its reproduction remains very limited.
sections.ecology: Its closest living relative is the Annamite striped rabbit (Nesolagus timminsi); the two are sister species within the genus.
sections.conservation: Deforestation and encroachment threaten known forest refuges, while the species remains too poorly surveyed for a confident population trend.
